name: Innervillgraten
kurzbeschreibung: Highest village in Osttirol, nestled in the sunny Villgratental, offering excellent cross-country skiing trails.
beschreibung:
Overview

Innervillgraten is nestled at an elevation of 1,402 metres in the high reaches of the Villgraten Valley in the district of Lienz, East Tyrol. Encircled by the rugged crests of the Villgraten Mountains, this expansive mountain municipality spans approximately 88 square kilometres and is home to around 900 inhabitants. Innervillgraten has deliberately dedicated itself to gentle, eco-conscious tourism, holding proud distinction as an official Mountaineering Village (Bergsteigerdorf) of the Alpine Clubs. Visitors will find no sprawling ski circus or crowded hotel resorts here; instead, the landscape is defined by centuries-old timber farmsteads weathered dark by the alpine sun, rushing torrents, and preserved alpine customs. The valley stands as a haven of authentic alpine tranquility, traditional mountain craftsmanship, and unspoiled wilderness.

History

Permanent settlement in the upper valley commenced during the Early Middle Ages through Slavic and Bavarian pioneers, with the earliest written record appearing in 1267 within deeds of the Prince-Bishopric of Brixen. For generations, the inhabitants survived through self-sufficiency amid harsh high-altitude conditions, relying on forestry, pastoral alpine farming, and sheep breeding. The neoclassical Parish Church of St. Martin in the village centre was constructed between 1806 and 1808. A renowned historical gem is the heritage-listed Oberstalleralm alpine village situated at 1,883 metres: Comprising 16 ancient log huts and the 1939 Visitation Chapel, the entire architectural ensemble enjoys strict monument protection. In the secluded side valley of Kalkstein stands the Maria Schnee (Our Lady of the Snows) pilgrimage chapel, built between 1658 and 1670 as a solemn vow during the plague.

Getting There

Innervillgraten is reached via the East Tyrolean road network. Drivers follow the federal road B100 through the Drau Valley from Lienz or from South Tyrol/San Candido towards Sillian and Heinfels. At Heinfels, the L273 Villgratental road branches off, climbing gently past Außervillgraten to reach Innervillgraten in roughly 15 minutes. Rail passengers travel via the Pustertal/Drau Valley line to Sillian railway station, where regular regional bus services (line 962) provide seamless connections into the heart of Innervillgraten and onward to Kalkstein.

Tips

A visit to the protected Oberstalleralm is essential, where weathered timber shingles and rustic chalets offer an enchanting glimpse into traditional alpine living. From there, scenic walking paths lead to the Unterstalleralm and the thundering Klapffall waterfall. For avid mountaineers, the Herz-Ass Trail is a premier highlight: This multi-day high-altitude trek traces a heart-shaped route around the valley rims, traversing over 50 alpine summits. Don't miss a stop at "Villgrater Natur" to discover how local raw sheep wool is processed into natural artisan bedding. In winter, the secluded valley is an internationally acclaimed sanctuary for backcountry ski touring and snowshoeing.
